facts.raw_span: A 43-year-old woman presented with abnormal vaginal bleeding
Family history was significant for prostate cancer in her father and paternal grandfather
No physical examination findings were explicitly mentioned in the case report
Dilation and curettage was performed
Tumor stained negative for MSH6 protein
MSI testing was negative
Germline mutation R1331X was detected in the MSH6 gene
A 43-year-old woman presented with abnormal vaginal bleeding
Family history was significant for prostate cancer in her father and paternal grandfather
No physical examination findings were explicitly mentioned in the case report
Dilation and curettage was performed
Tumor stained negative for MSH6 protein
MSI testing was negative
Germline mutation R1331X was detected in the MSH6 gene

concepts.why: The patient's family history of prostate cancer and her own germline mutation in the MSH6 gene suggest Lynch syndrome.
The patient presented with abnormal vaginal bleeding and underwent dilation and curettage, which are consistent with endometrial cancer.
The patient's tumor stained negative for MSH6 protein and she has a germline mutation in the MSH6 gene, which suggests MSH6-related endometrial cancer.
The patient presented with abnormal vaginal bleeding and underwent dilation and curettage, which are consistent with atypical endometrial hyperplasia.

rationales.F01: Abnormal vaginal bleeding is a common symptom of endometrial cancer and atypical endometrial hyperplasia.
rationales.F02: Family history of prostate cancer may be related to Lynch syndrome.
rationales.F05: Negative MSH6 protein staining suggests that the tumor may not be related to MSH6 deficiency.
rationales.F06: Negative MSI testing suggests that the tumor may not have high microsatellite instability, which is often seen in Lynch syndrome.
rationales.F07: Germline mutation R1331X in the MSH6 gene is a strong indicator of Lynch syndrome and MSH6-related endometrial cancer.

frontier_selector.rationale: Germline mutation R1331X in the MSH6 gene and negative MSH6 protein staining support MSH6-related endometrial cancer, with Lynch syndrome as a possible underlying condition due to family history of prostate cancer.
